object.medium: Serenade for strings; autograph score, ink on paper
object.description: Mozart entered this serenade for strings in his personal catalogue on 10 August 1787 in Vienna, while he was in the middle of composing the opera Don Giovanni. He called it simply 'Eine kleine Nacht Musik', a little night music, meaning a short serenade of the kind played outdoors at evening entertainments. Nobody knows who commissioned it or when it was first played, and the work was not published until 1827, long after his death. Its opening fanfare, rising through a G major chord, has since become one of the most recognised phrases in Western music. The page shown is the first leaf of Mozart's own manuscript, written quickly and almost without corrections. The visitor hears the first movement, Allegro, in a recording by the Advent Chamber Orchestra from its 2005-06 season, released under a Creative Commons licence.
facts: Mozart's catalogue lists five movements; the second, a minuet, is lost, so the serenade is almost always heard in four.
The manuscript was sold by Mozart's widow Constanze to the publisher Johann Anton André in 1799, and was first printed in 1827.
The title in Mozart's catalogue is 'Eine kleine Nacht Musik, bestehend in einem Allegro, Menuett und Trio, Romance, Menuett und Trio, und Finale'.
